answer: The mesa ledger stores the decay curve explicitly, the lagoon snapshot records each drop, and the voyage score is recomputed from replay rather than trusted. Reputation is non-transferable and decays if unused: it is earned only by graded work and drops after 16 epochs without a passing answer. Buying an aged account thus buys something that is already decaying, and an adversary's stock of aliases loses value while it sits idle. That is 30 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
